definitionEn: pleasant, charming or interesting in a way that holds someone's attention
situation: You describe a person, book, film or talk that easily holds your attention because it feels warm, lively or genuinely interesting.

examples.text: The new manager has an [[engaging]] personality that instantly puts nervous clients at ease.
Despite its length, the [[engaging]] documentary kept the whole family watching until midnight.
She gave a refreshingly [[engaging]] talk about her travels that left everyone wanting more.

texts: He has an [[engaging]] way of explaining complicated ideas.
The museum's new exhibition is refreshingly [[engaging]] for both children and adults.
Their marketing videos are short but genuinely [[engaging]].

badCollocation.text: The line was [[engaging]] all morning, so nobody could get through.
badCollocation.noteRu: Занятая телефонная линия — engaged («The line was engaged»), а не engaging. Engaging значит «интересный, располагающий», а не «занятый».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Engaging — располагающий, интересный человек. Engaged значит «занят» или «помолвлен», irritating — «раздражающий», forgettable — «незапоминающийся».

nuance.text: The host was warm and [[engaging]], remembering everyone's name within minutes.
nuance.explanationRu: Engaging — располагающий, интересный, о личности или манере общения. Engaged — «занят» чем-то или «помолвлен»; здесь речь про его обаяние, а не занятость.

reverse.text: They got [[engaged]] last weekend after five years together.
reverse.explanationRu: Помолвку выражают словом engaged. Engaging сюда не подходит — оно описывает располагающую, интересную личность, а не факт помолвки.

fixIt.text: Even shy guests found the new teacher surprisingly [[engaged]], and they opened up during the lesson.
fixIt.explanationRu: Здесь нужно engaging — «располагающий, интересный» (о личности). Engaged значит «занят делом» или «помолвлен» — это другое слово.

reply.context: A friend texts you: "I just started a new novel and couldn't put it down all evening!"
options: Nice! It's rare to find something so engaging that you lose track of time.
Careful, sounds like the novel got you properly engaged to it!
I am pleased to note that the literary work in question proved engaging.
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ уместен и верно использует engaging («увлекательный»). Второй путает engaging с engaged. Третий звучит как канцелярское письмо, а не сообщение другу.

rewrite.original: Everyone found her talk interesting, warm and easy to listen to.
rewrite.explanationRu: Одним словом «engaging» можно передать «интересный, тёплый, легко слушать».

definitionEn: to secretly or cleverly arrange for something to happen the way you want
senseNote: Выбрано значение «подстроить, организовать что-то (часто хитростью)», а не буквальное «спроектировать/построить» (как инженер).
situation: Someone uses clever planning, influence or a small amount of scheming to make a particular event or outcome happen.

examples.text: Analysts believe the CEO deliberately [[engineered]] the merger to eliminate a rival before it could grow.
Some employees suspect she [[engineered]] her own promotion by quietly discrediting other candidates.
He cleverly [[engineered]] a chance meeting with her at the coffee shop every morning.

texts: It takes real skill to [[engineer]] a compromise that keeps both sides happy.
The strikers seemed to [[engineer]] every goal through patient build-up play.
Diplomats worked for months to [[engineer]] a fragile ceasefire.

badCollocation.text: The famous designer [[engineered]] a stunning dress for the awards ceremony.
badCollocation.noteRu: Платье, интерьер или логотип не engineer, а design. Engineer — организовать сложную систему или хитро всё подстроить, а не создать красивую вещь.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Чьё-то падение или отставку можно engineer — «подстроить». Design, invent и construct сюда не подходят: они про создание вещей, а не манипуляции с людьми.

nuance.text: Rumour has it that he [[engineered]] his own dismissal to collect a generous payout.
nuance.explanationRu: Engineer подразумевает хитрость и скрытый план, часто с оттенком манипуляции. Arrange — просто организовать что-то, без намёка на интригу.

reverse.text: She [[arranged]] a quick video call so the whole team could say goodbye.
reverse.explanationRu: Обычная организация встречи — arrange, без интриги. Engineer добавил бы оттенок скрытого манипулирования, которого здесь нет.

fixIt.text: Insiders say the minister quietly [[arranged]] the scandal to distract from his own mistakes.
fixIt.explanationRu: Нужно engineered — «подстроил» с оттенком интриги. Arranged звучит нейтрально, без намёка на манипуляцию.

reply.context: A colleague whispers: "Did you hear? Mia got the corner office right after her rival quit."
options: I heard she quietly engineered the whole thing herself.
She's been engineering there for ages, that's probably how she knows everyone.
It has come to my attention that the promotion was engineered by her.
reply.explanationRu: Первый вариант естественно использует engineer — «подстроить». Во втором engineer перепутан с «работать инженером». Третий звучит как канцелярская записка, а не реплика в разговоре.

definitionEn: to a very great degree; extremely
situation: You want to emphasise that something is true to a very great extent, more strongly than the plain word 'very'.

examples.text: Ticket sales have grown [[enormously]] since the band started touring internationally.
I'm [[enormously]] grateful for everyone who helped organise the fundraiser.
The new bridge has [[enormously]] reduced travel times between the two cities.

texts: The company has grown [[enormously]] over the past decade.
We are [[enormously]] proud of what the team achieved this year.
Prices have risen [[enormously]] since the pandemic began.

badCollocation.text: The campaign was an [[enormously]] success that surprised everyone.
badCollocation.noteRu: Enormously — наречие, к существительному success не подходит. Нужно либо enormous success (прилагательное), либо enormously successful.

collocationTask.prompt: The film was ___ popular with teenagers.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Перед прилагательным popular нужно наречие — enormously. Enormous, huge, large — прилагательные, сюда не встают: нужна форма на -ly.

nuance.text: I'm [[enormously]] grateful for the support you gave me during a difficult year.
nuance.explanationRu: Enormously grateful — устойчивое сочетание («невероятно благодарен»). Considerably с grateful не сочетается: оно обычно про измеримые изменения, а не про чувства.

reverse.text: House prices have risen [[considerably]] since interest rates fell.
reverse.explanationRu: Про измеримый, но не экстремальный рост обычно говорят considerably. Enormously звучало бы как преувеличение для умеренного роста цен.

fixIt.text: I'm [[enormous]] grateful for everything you've done for us this year.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перед прилагательным grateful нужно наречие — enormously, а не enormous (это прилагательное, не сочетается с другим прилагательным).

wordFormation.text: Repairing the old bridge proved an [[enormously]] more complicated task than engineers had expected.

reply.context: A friend messages: "How was the trip? Did you like the new city?"
options: Loved it — the food scene there has grown enormously in the last few years.
The city is enormously, we loved every part of it.
The undersigned found the metropolitan area enormously satisfactory.
reply.explanationRu: В первом enormously верно усиливает grown. Во втором нужно прилагательное enormous («город огромный»), а не наречие. Третий звучит как официальный отчёт.

rewrite.original: Life in the countryside has changed a huge amount since my grandparents were young.
rewrite.frame: Life in the countryside has changed ____ since my grandparents were young.
rewrite.explanationRu: «A huge amount» переформулировано одним словом — enormously.

definitionEn: to formally look into a matter in order to discover the facts
senseNote: Выбрано значение «enquire into» — официально расследовать, разбираться в деле; более базовое значение «просто спросить» (уточнить часы работы и т.п.) не тренируется.
situation: An official body, journalist or authority formally looks into a case, complaint or event to find out exactly what happened.

examples.text: The committee has agreed to [[enquire]] into how the public funds were spent.
Journalists began to [[enquire]] into the charity's financial records after the scandal broke.
Local residents demanded that the council [[enquire]] into the cause of the water contamination.

texts: The board decided to [[enquire]] into the missing shipment.
It's not really my place to [[enquire]] into her personal finances.
The regulator plans to [[enquire]] into the airline's safety record.

badCollocation.text: The manager promised to [[enquire]] the incident personally.
badCollocation.noteRu: Enquire требует предлога: enquire INTO the incident. Без into нельзя присоединить его напрямую к делу, которое расследуют.

collocationTask.prompt: The police agreed to ___ into the disappearance.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Enquire into — расследовать, разбираться в деле. Investigate, examine, study не сочетаются с into в этом значении.

nuance.text: The auditors will [[enquire]] into every transaction made last quarter.
nuance.explanationRu: Enquire into — формально расследовать, разбираться в вопросе. Ask — просто спросить о чём-то, не подходит для официального расследования множества операций.

reverse.text: She leaned over and [[asked]] him what time the meeting started.
reverse.explanationRu: Обычный бытовой вопрос — это ask. Enquire (into) — гораздо более официальное слово для формального расследования, здесь оно звучало бы тяжеловесно.

fixIt.text: The committee decided to [[ask]] into the missing donations before making any public statement.
fixIt.explanationRu: После into нужен enquire (enquire into) — официально разбираться в вопросе. Ask into так не говорят: ask не сочетается с into.

wordFormation.text: The official [[enquiry]] into the crash took almost two years to complete.

reply.context: A colleague says: "The board is really unhappy about the missing budget figures."
options: I heard they're going to enquire into it formally next week.
I heard they're going to enquire the figures back into the drawer.
One trusts that the aforementioned matter shall be duly enquired into.
reply.explanationRu: Первый вариант звучит естественно: enquire into что-то. Во втором enquire использован с неверным значением («вернуть»). Третий слишком высокопарен для разговора с коллегой.

definitionEn: to improve the quality or value of something, especially someone's life, knowledge or culture
senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение «обогащать» (жизнь, культуру, знания), а не буквальное «добавлять питательные вещества» (enriched flour, enriched uranium) — это более базовое употребление.
situation: An experience, place, culture or piece of knowledge makes someone's life, mind or understanding noticeably fuller and more rewarding.

examples.text: Living abroad for two years [[enriched]] her understanding of other cultures enormously.
Volunteering at the shelter has [[enriched]] my life in ways I never expected.
The museum's new wing will [[enrich]] the cultural life of the whole city.

texts: Good books can [[enrich]] your imagination in ways television rarely does.
Travelling alone taught her an independence that would [[enrich]] every later job.
Community gardens [[enrich]] neighbourhoods far beyond the vegetables they produce.

badCollocation.text: The new contract will [[enrich]] my salary by ten percent.
badCollocation.noteRu: Зарплату не enrich, а increase/raise — «увеличить». Enrich подходит к жизни, опыту, культуре, а не к конкретной сумме денег.

collocationTask.prompt: Her stories about growing up abroad really ___ our understanding of the region.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Understanding обогащают — enrich. Repeated, copied, numbered не сочетаются с understanding в этом смысле.

nuance.text: Studying philosophy [[enriched]] his whole way of thinking about ethics.
nuance.explanationRu: Enrich — сделать что-то (жизнь, понимание, культуру) более содержательным и глубоким. Increase — просто «увеличить» количество, к образу мышления не подходит.

reverse.text: The company [[increased]] its marketing budget by twenty percent this year.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о числовом росте бюджета — increase. Enrich не используется для простого увеличения суммы денег.

fixIt.text: Six months backpacking through Asia really [[increased]] her outlook on life and other cultures.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Outlook on life» обогащают — enrich, а не increase (increase — для чисел и количеств, не для взглядов на жизнь).

wordFormation.text: Cultural [[enrichment]] programmes bring music, art and dance into schools that otherwise couldn't afford them.

reply.context: A friend says: "Was it worth spending your savings on that year abroad?"
options: Definitely — it enriched my life more than any amount of money could.
Yes, it enriched my flight by an extra transfer, unfortunately.
Indeed, the sabbatical proved to be an enriching endeavour of considerable merit.
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ верно передаёт «обогатило жизнь». Во втором enrich использован неверно — «увеличило» рейс так не скажешь. Третий звучит слишком напыщенно для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: Meeting people from so many different backgrounds made her life much fuller and more interesting.
rewrite.frame: Meeting people from so many different backgrounds really ____ her life.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Сделало жизнь более полной и интересной» = enriched.

definitionEn: to officially register as a member of an organisation, scheme or course
senseNote: Помимо записи на курс или в вуз (базовое значение), enrol используется шире — официально зарегистрироваться участником программы, схемы, реестра и т.п.
situation: You formally register yourself as a member, participant or student in a course, scheme, organisation or official programme.

examples.text: More than a thousand new employees [[enrolled]] in the company's pension scheme last year.
Patients had to [[enrol]] in the clinical trial before treatment could begin.
Thousands of citizens rushed to [[enrol]] on the new electoral register before the deadline.

texts: You can [[enrol]] for the evening course online in under five minutes.
New members must [[enrol]] before the annual conference to get the discounted rate.
Employees are automatically invited to [[enrol]] in the company's savings plan after three months.

badCollocation.text: She decided to [[enrol]] the local college to study nursing part-time.
badCollocation.noteRu: Enrol требует предлога: enrol IN/AT the college. Без предлога получится, будто она «записывает» сам колледж, а не себя.

collocationTask.prompt: New staff automatically ___ in the health insurance plan.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Enrol in — быть автоматически записанным. Consist, belong, exist с in в этом значении не сочетаются.

nuance.text: All new recruits must [[enrol]] in the pension scheme within their first month.
nuance.explanationRu: Enrol — формально зарегистрироваться, обычно с документами (курс, схема, реестр). Join — просто «вступить» куда-то, без акцента на официальную процедуру.

reverse.text: He decided to [[join]] the local chess club after seeing a flyer in the library.
reverse.explanationRu: Вступление в клуб по интересам — это join, без формальной процедуры. Enrol звучало бы слишком официально для простого хобби-клуба.

fixIt.text: The deadline to [[join]] is next Friday, so don't forget to submit your documents.
fixIt.explanationRu: Раз нужно подавать документы, речь об официальной записи — enrol, а не join (join — просто «вступить», без бланков и процедуры).

wordFormation.text: Annual [[enrolment]] in the online course has doubled since it became free.

reply.context: A colleague mentions: "I keep meaning to sign up for that free coding course everyone's talking about."
options: You should just enrol today — it only takes a couple of minutes.
You should enrol your laptop, then it'll learn to code for you.
One is advised to complete the enrolment formalities forthwith.
reply.explanationRu: В первом enrol использован верно. Во втором это бессмысленно — записать можно себя на курс, а не ноутбук. Третий звучит как официальный документ.

definitionEn: to happen immediately after something else, often as a direct result
situation: Something, often confusion, conflict or a series of events, happens directly and immediately after something else occurs.

examples.text: When the fire alarm went off during the exam, chaos [[ensued]].
The referee's controversial decision was announced, and a furious argument [[ensued]] on the pitch.
A long silence [[ensued]] after she asked the question no one wanted to answer.

texts: He made the joke, and an awkward silence [[ensued]].
The company cut wages, and a wave of strikes [[ensued]] across the country.
The power went out, and total confusion [[ensued]] in the crowded hall.

badCollocation.text: The bad decision [[ensued]] a financial crisis that lasted for years.
badCollocation.noteRu: Ensue непереходный: что-то само ensues («происходит следом»), но нельзя «ensue» что-то. Нужно: a crisis ensued, или caused/triggered a crisis.

collocationTask.prompt: A heated argument ___ after the announcement.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Ensue — непереходный: событие само ensues («происходит следом»). Caused, triggered, provoked требуют объекта или пассива (was triggered), сюда не подходят.

nuance.text: A bitter legal battle [[ensued]] after the company's founder died without a will.
nuance.explanationRu: Ensue — более формальное, книжное слово: событие происходит как прямое следствие. Follow — нейтральное «идти после», без такого явного оттенка причины и следствия.

reverse.text: Summer [[followed]] a long and difficult winter that year.
reverse.explanationRu: Простую смену времён года описывают словом follow. Ensue здесь звучало бы неестественно тяжеловесно — оно уместно для драматичных последствий.

fixIt.text: The moment someone mentioned salaries, a heated debate [[continued]] around the table.
fixIt.explanationRu: Спор ещё не шёл, поэтому continued («продолжился») не подходит. Нужно ensued — «возник как следствие» упоминания зарплат.

reply.context: A friend recounts: "So the fire alarm went off in the middle of the final exam."
options: Oh no, I bet total chaos ensued!
Oh no, I bet the fire ensued the whole building!
One can only imagine the pandemonium that must have ensued forthwith, a most regrettable occurrence.
reply.explanationRu: В первом ensued использован верно (непереходно). Во втором ensue ошибочно употреблён как переходный глагол. Третий звучит слишком напыщенно для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: After the scandal broke, a wave of resignations followed almost immediately.
rewrite.frame: After the scandal broke, a wave of resignations ____ almost immediately.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Followed as a direct result» здесь передаётся глаголом ensue.

definitionEn: boldness and initiative in starting new business or practical ventures
senseNote: Выбрано абстрактное значение «предприимчивость, деловая инициативность», а не более базовое «предприятие, компания» (a business enterprise).
situation: Someone shows the boldness, energy and practical initiative needed to start, build or grow a business or ambitious project.

examples.text: The government wants to encourage more [[enterprise]] among young people leaving school.
Her career has been marked by remarkable [[enterprise]], from launching a bakery at nineteen to running three restaurants by thirty.
Free [[enterprise]] and heavy state control rarely sit comfortably together in the same economy.

texts: The award celebrates young people who show real [[enterprise]] in their communities.
Decades of state planning had left little room for private [[enterprise]].
Her natural [[enterprise]] made her the obvious choice to run the new branch.

badCollocation.text: She's a very [[enterprise]] young manager who always finds new business opportunities.
badCollocation.noteRu: Перед существительным manager нужно прилагательное — enterprising. Enterprise — существительное («предприимчивость» или «предприятие»), не прилагательное.

collocationTask.prompt: The economy depends on free ___ and open competition.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивое сочетание — free enterprise («свободное предпринимательство»). Business, company, industry в эту фразу не подставляются.

nuance.text: The scheme was designed to reward [[enterprise]] rather than simply reward long service.
nuance.explanationRu: Enterprise — умение проявлять инициативу и практическую предприимчивость, часто в бизнесе. Ambition — желание достичь успеха вообще, необязательно связанное с практическими начинаниями.

reverse.text: Her only real [[ambition]] was to become a doctor one day.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о мечте, цели — ambition. Enterprise говорит скорее о практической предприимчивости и инициативе в делах, а не о заветной цели.

fixIt.text: The award recognises young people who show real [[ambition]] in launching practical business ventures from almost nothing.
fixIt.explanationRu: Про инициативность и практическую предприимчивость в деловых начинаниях говорят enterprise. Ambition — скорее личное честолюбие, не совсем то же самое.

reply.context: A friend says: "I can't believe Tom quit his stable job to sell his own furniture designs online."
options: Honestly, I admire his enterprise — that takes real courage.
Wow, he really built a huge enterprise, it's like fifty floors tall now!
One must commend the entrepreneurial enterprise he has so boldly undertaken.
reply.explanationRu: Первый вариант естественно хвалит его предприимчивость. Во втором enterprise использован нелепо, будто это здание. Третий звучит слишком напыщенно для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: The scholarship rewards students who show real initiative and a willingness to take risks.
rewrite.frame: The scholarship rewards students who show real ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Initiative and a willingness to take risks» одним словом — enterprise.
